## About

This reading group works through *Mostly Harmless Econometrics*
(Angrist and Pischke, 2009) and related readings, organized around one idea:

> An estimator is not a research design.

Every session follows the same sequence of questions:

**Question → Specification & Estimand → Identification → Estimation → Inference**

The methods change from session to session. The sequence of questions does not.

## Tentative topics

1. A course correction in the history of econometrics
2. Regression and selection on observables
3. Instrumental variables and LATE
4. Difference-in-differences
5. Regression discontinuity
6. Panel data
7. Treatment-effect heterogeneity
8. Structural models and policy counterfactuals

Slides, readings, and recordings for each meeting are on the [Sessions](sessions.qmd) page.

## Core readings

- Angrist, J. D., and J.-S. Pischke (2009).
  *Mostly Harmless Econometrics: An Empiricist's Companion*. Princeton University Press.
- Lewbel, A. (2019). "The Identification Zoo: Meanings of Identification in Econometrics."
  *Journal of Economic Literature*, 57(4), 835–903.
  [doi:10.1257/jel.20181361](https://doi.org/10.1257/jel.20181361)
